why: the validation harness, asked about an animal it holds no parameters for

result.reason: this reference set covers Teleostei, and Mus musculus is outside it (the NCBI taxonomy places it inside Mus <subgenus>, Mus <genus>, Murinae, Muridae). No nearest relative is reported, because the nearest shape in a reference set that does not cover the animal is not a relative of it -- it is the least bad row in the wrong table. This is cannot-assess, not a measurement that failed.
result.what_is_missing: a body-shape reference set covering the design's clade, with its own out-of-distribution calibration
result.basis: FishShapes v1 (doi 10.1002/ecy.3829) is 16 377 TELEOST specimens, and the fin axis is 9 beloniform species (Daane et al. 2021 sheet A). There is no non-teleost shape reference in this project.

provenance.source: doi 10.1002/ecy.3829; Zenodo 6642650 -- not used for this query, which is outside its clade

result.scope: Nearest real relatives in a 6-feature body space (FishShapes v1, 16 377 teleost specimens, measured; our 3 real organisms and their ontogeny stages) and on pectoral fin length (Daane 2021 sheet A, 9 beloniform species, measured). The other fin features have only our own two lineages as references, so they get an uncalibrated envelope rule. Distance is not relatedness: a nearest neighbour is the most similar shape, not an ancestor. Birds (Aves) excluded: frozen holdout. THIS CALL RETURNED NO COMPARISON: the reference set does not cover the design's clade, which is reported as cannot-assess rather than as a distant neighbour.
